date_note: Date Bitdefender published its research; the page gives no earlier day.
title: Bitdefender: fake GTA VI PC client site uses ClickFix to deliver a likely Rust-based stealer
summary: Bitdefender Labs says a website posing as a GTA VI PC streaming client offers a ZIP containing GTA6Cloud.exe or a Win+R PowerShell command, and that its analysis found the command leads to malware. Bitdefender calls the payload a likely new or modified Rust-based stealer that targets browser credentials, Discord, Steam, crypto-wallet data and AI or developer API keys. Bitdefender notes no official PC version is available.
plain: Bitdefender says a fake site offering GTA VI for PC leads to password-stealing malware. It says there is no official PC version.
exec: Gamers' browser logins, wallets and developer keys are the stated targets, which can spill into work accounts.
action: Bitdefender advises: if you pasted the command into Run, treat the computer as compromised, disconnect it, scan it and change passwords from a clean device; check game availability through the publisher's official channels.

validation.note: Bitdefender Labs' own research post read; Begeek (27 November) restates it.
